vocabulary.meaning_en: to give good reasons for what you think or do
vocabulary.example: Can you justify this decision?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to refuse to change your position when people pressure you
vocabulary.example: She stood her ground and didn't make the call.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something it is your job to do or deal with
vocabulary.example: This is your responsibility, not mine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: at the beginning; originally
vocabulary.example: It was your decision in the first place.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to think again about something in order to change it
vocabulary.example: I've been rethinking our plans.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the number of workers a company has
vocabulary.example: We need to look at our staffing levels.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make a mistake when calculating or judging something
vocabulary.example: I miscalculated the costs.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to do something wrong
vocabulary.note_ar: نقول make a mistake وليس do a mistake.
vocabulary.example: Sorry, I made a mistake.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a mistake (more formal)
vocabulary.example: There is an error in the report.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give someone their old job back
vocabulary.example: The company reinstated her after a week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to change a decision to the opposite
vocabulary.example: The manager reversed his decision.

vocabulary.meaning_en: done too quickly without enough thought
vocabulary.example: Maybe I was a bit hasty.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to spend less money
vocabulary.example: We closed the shop to save money.

vocabulary.meaning_en: paper, pens and other things for writing in an office
vocabulary.note_ar: لا تخلط بينها وبين stationary (ثابت). كلتاهما تُنطقان بالطريقة نفسها.
vocabulary.example: Nobody has ordered any stationery.

vocabulary.meaning_en: keeping yourself and things clean
vocabulary.example: Good hygiene is important in a kitchen.

vocabulary.meaning_en: difficult and embarrassing
vocabulary.example: It was an awkward phone call.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who is not brave
vocabulary.example: Don't be a coward – tell him the truth.

vocabulary.meaning_en: what you say is partly right
vocabulary.example: I suppose you have a point.

vocabulary.meaning_en: approved by the people in charge
vocabulary.example: The news is better coming from you, to make it official.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an increase in salary
vocabulary.example: She asked for a pay rise.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a written legal agreement
vocabulary.example: Let's hope we don't lose that contract.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to buy from another company
vocabulary.example: If you're late, customers will go elsewhere.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to phone someone who called you
vocabulary.example: Nobody returned their call yesterday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who was your boss before
vocabulary.example: I met my ex-boss at the conference.

fine_lines.title: stationery vs stationary
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الكلمتان لهما النطق نفسه. stationery (بحرف e) تعني الأدوات المكتبية كالورق والأقلام. stationary (بحرف a) صفة تعني ثابتًا لا يتحرك. للتذكر: e مثل envelope (ظرف).
fine_lines.explanation_en: They sound the same. Stationery (with e) = paper, pens, envelopes. Stationary (with a) = not moving.

examples.sentence: The car was stationary at the lights.

fine_lines.title: mistake vs error
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعنى واحد: خطأ. mistake أكثر شيوعًا في الحديث اليومي، و error أكثر رسمية وتُستخدم في الأنظمة والحسابات. نقول make a mistake و make an error.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean something wrong. Mistake is more common; error is more formal or technical.

examples.sentence: I made a mistake with your name.
The computer shows an error message.

expressions.phrase: You're the boss and I think the news is better coming from you.
expressions.meaning_ar: أنت المدير، وأظن أن من الأفضل أن يأتي الخبر منك.
expressions.meaning_en: You are in charge, so you should give the news.
expressions.example: You're the manager, and I think the news is better coming from you.

expressions.phrase: It was your decision in the first place, so you need to explain that the situation has changed.
expressions.meaning_ar: كان القرار قرارك من البداية، لذا عليك أن تشرح أن الوضع قد تغيّر.
expressions.meaning_en: You made the decision, so you should explain the change.
expressions.example: It was your decision in the first place, so you need to tell the client.

expressions.meaning_en: It is your job to deal with this.
expressions.example: I'm sorry, but this is your responsibility.

expressions.phrase: I've been rethinking our staffing situation in the office.
expressions.meaning_ar: كنت أعيد التفكير في وضع الموظفين في المكتب.
expressions.meaning_en: I've been thinking again about how many staff we need.
expressions.example: I've been rethinking our plans for next year.

expressions.phrase: Sorry, I made a mistake. I miscalculated my staffing numbers.
expressions.meaning_ar: آسف، لقد أخطأت. أخطأت في تقدير عدد الموظفين الذي نحتاجه.
expressions.meaning_en: An apology for a wrong decision.
expressions.example: Sorry, I made a mistake. I miscalculated the delivery date.

expressions.phrase: I would love to have you back in the office.
expressions.meaning_ar: يسعدني جدًا أن تعود إلى المكتب.
expressions.meaning_en: I really want you to return to work here.
expressions.example: We would love to have you back on the team.

expressions.phrase: I suppose you have a point.
expressions.example: I suppose you have a point. Let's wait until Monday.

expressions.phrase: Maybe I was a bit hasty.
expressions.example: Maybe I was a bit hasty when I said no.

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous: I've been + -ing
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم have/has been + فعل بـ ing لعمل بدأ في الماضي واستمر حتى الآن: I've been rethinking... (كنت أفكر من فترة وما زلت).
grammar.explanation_en: Use have/has been + -ing for an activity that started in the past and continues until now.
examples: I've been rethinking our staffing situation.
We've been waiting for your call.
She has been working here for ten years.

grammar.title: Firm but polite: You need to... / This is your...
grammar.explanation_ar: للتمسك بموقفك بأدب: ابدأ بحقيقة (You're the boss)، ثم استخدم I think لتلطيف الرأي، و You need to لتوضيح الواجب.
grammar.explanation_en: To stand your ground politely: state a fact, soften with 'I think', then say 'you need to'.
examples: You're the boss and I think the news is better coming from you.
You need to explain that the situation has changed.

grammar.title: would love to + verb
grammar.explanation_ar: would love to أقوى وأدفأ من would like to، وتعبّر عن رغبة حقيقية بأدب.
grammar.explanation_en: 'Would love to' is warmer and stronger than 'would like to'.
examples: I would love to have you back in the office.
We would love to work with you.

questions.question: I've been ___ our staffing situation.
questions.explanation_ar: نستخدم I've been + فعل بصيغة ing.

questions.question: Paul gives Denise her job back. He ___ her.
questions.explanation_en: Reinstate means give the job back.

questions.question: We need to order paper and pens. We need ___.
questions.explanation_en: Stationery (with e) is paper and pens.

questions.question: It was your decision in the first ___.
questions.explanation_ar: in the first place = في الأصل.
questions.explanation_en: The phrase is 'in the first place'.

questions.question: 'I miscalculated' means ___.
choices: I made a mistake in my calculation or judgement

questions.question: Which phrase is the warmest?
choices: I would love to have you back.
questions.explanation_ar: would love to تعبير دافئ ومهذب.
questions.explanation_en: 'Would love to' is warm and polite.

questions.question: 'Maybe I was a bit hasty' means ___.
Anna says: 'This is your ___.' She means Paul must deal with it.
